How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment
for agenda items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per
person (six minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time
limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note
that interactions between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings
are subject to the City’s Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – APRIL 2026

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2025-2026 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 25-25) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment

  D. AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR COUNCIL CHAMBER AUDIOVISUAL UPGRADE
  (SENATE BILL 707) – NOT TO EXCEED $117,666

  Staff issued Request for Proposals (RFP 26-03) on March 18, 2026, for the
  upgrade and modernization of the City Council Chamber audiovisual (AV)
  system. Based on evaluation criteria, Western Audio Visual & Security was
  determined to provide the best overall value to the City. The proposed project
  will modernize the City’s AV infrastructure to support reliable in-person and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 19, 2026  3
   remote participation and enhance accessibility in alignment with Senate Bill 707
  requirements.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council award a contract to Western Audio
  Visual & Security for the Council Chamber audiovisual system upgrade in an
  amount not to exceed $117,666, which includes a base project cost of
  $93,810.70 and a contingency for voting system integration, if required, and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.

  E. SEVENTH AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT
  WITH ARAKELIAN ENTERPRISES, INCORPORATED, DOING BUSINESS AS
  ATHENS SERVICES, FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A THIRD RECYCLING
  BIN AND RATE ADJUSTMENT FOR COMMERCIAL ACCOUNTS

  The City has contracted with Arakelian Enterprises, Incorporated, doing
  business as Athens Services, for refuse disposal-related services since May 5,
  1987, when City Council approved assigning Athens the contract held by the
  San Gabriel Disposal Company, whose owner was retiring and proposed the
  transfer. The Amended and Restated Agreement was executed on October 17,
  2000, and has been amended six times since then. The Seventh Amendment
  transitions to a 3-bin system, modernizes rate structures and annual adjustment
  mechanism to account for costs such as container procurement, route
  adjustment, and increased collection frequency.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Review and approve the proposed Seventh Amendment to the Amended
  and Restated Agreement with Arakelian Enterprises, Incorporated, doing
  business as Athens Services;

  2. Direct staff to conduct a Proposition 218-compliant majority protest process
  including scheduling a public hearing and mail notices to affected parcel
  owners of record at least 45-days in advance of the hearing; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 19, 2026  4
   3. Authorize staff to conduct Proposition 218-compliant community education
  prior to public hearing.

  F. FIRST AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  INDIGO CIVIL ENGINEERING, INCORPORATED FOR DESIGN AND
  ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES ON THE VINCENT LUGO PARK ACCESS
  PATH AND PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE REPLACEMENT PROJECT

  The City was awarded a grant of $401,170 through the Los Angeles County
  Regional Park and Open Space District Measure A Grant Program for the
  Vincent Lugo Park Access Path and Pedestrian Bridge Replacement Project
  (Project) to improve the pedestrian path from Vincent Lugo Park to Hovey
  Avenue and renovate the existing pedestrian bridge over the Alhambra Wash.
  On August 20, 2024, following a request for proposals, City Council approved a
  Professional Services Agreement with Indigo Civil Engineering, Incorporated
  (Indigo) to provide professional design and engineering services for the Project
  in an amount not-to-exceed $63,160, plus a 10% contingency. Based upon
  further needs that were identified during this initial project phase, staff
  requested a change order proposal from Indigo to provide additional services.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as it has no
  reasonable potential for significantly impacting the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Amendment No. 1 to the Professional Services Agreement with
  Indigo Civil Engineering, Incorporated for design and engineering services
  to increase the not-to-exceed amount to $92,160, plus a 10% contingency
  of $9,216; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 1, approve
  increasing Purchase Order No. 9370 for the amended agreement to $92,160,
  and approve increasing Purchase Order No. 9371 for the contingency to
  $9,216.

  G. APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT TO THE AGREEMENT FOR A RETAINER WITH
  ARTS CONSULTING GROUP AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 26-21
  APPROPRIATING $30,000 FROM THE CITY’S GENERAL FUND

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 19, 2026  5
   In March 2026, the City Council approved the Mission Playhouse draft strategic
  plan completed by Arts Consulting Group and directed staff to bring forward a
  contract for a retainer for operational modeling, implementation support, etc.
  with that same consultant. Included in this report is a brief summary of the work
  to be included as part of the retainer and the amendment to the initial
  agreement with Arts Consulting Group.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Amendment to the agreement with Arts Consulting Group for
  a retainer for a period of six (6) months; and

  2. Adopt Resolution No. 26-21 appropriating $30,000 from the City’s Fiscal
  Year 2025-2026 General Fund budget.

  H. THEATRE FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY SAN GABRIEL UNIFIED SCHOOL
  DISTRICT FOR DEL MAR HIGH SCHOOL GRADUATION

  San Gabriel Unified School District is requesting a fee waiver for the Del Mar
  High School graduation ceremony, scheduled to take place June 3, 2026, at the
  Mission Playhouse. The request is for a $2,317.50 reduction to reduce their
  rental cost to $3,291.75.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve staff’s recommendation to
  grant a waiver of the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse building/facility rental and
  equipment usage fees in the amount of $2,317.50 for the June 3, 2026, Del Mar
  High School Graduation.

  I. AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (LACDA) FOR LEAD FREE HOMES LA

  The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA), on behalf of Los
  Angeles County and its participating cities, administers a program called Lead

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 19, 2026  6
   Free Homes LA. Lead Free Homes LA provides free lead-paint hazard mitigation
  services to eligible residential properties, with the goal of protecting children
  under six from lead exposure. To provide this service to residents of the City of
  San Gabriel, an agreement between the City of San Gabriel and LACDA is
  necessary.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the agreement between the Los Angeles County Development Authority
  (LACDA) and the City of San Gabriel.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCES NO. 728 AND NO. 729 AMENDING TO UPDATE THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW FOR URBAN
  DWELLING UNITS (ZTA25-001), ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS AND
  JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS (ZTA26-001) – INTRODUCTION
  AND FIRST READING

  The California Legislature adopted Senate Bills 450, 544, and 1211 and
  Assembly Bills 130, 462, and 1154 in 2024 and 2025, amending existing State
  law pertaining to Urban Dwelling Units, Accessory Dwelling Units, and Junior
  Accessory Dwelling Units. Draft ordinances were provided to the Planning
  Commission for consideration and recommendation on July 14, 2025 and
  February 9, 2026. Following discussion, the Planning Commission
  recommended approval to the City Council of the proposed Zone Text
  Amendments (ZTA25-001 and ZTA26-001) for Ordinances No. 728 and No. 729.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines, the
  amendment to a Zoning Ordinance is not considered a project as defined in
  Section 15378 and can be seen with certainty that it will not have a significant
  effect on the environment. The proposed amendment to the Zoning Ordinance
  qualifies for this CEQA exemption as there is no possibility that the ordinance will
  have a significant effect on the environment as it amends the City’s Municipal
  Code to demonstrate compliance with State Accessory Dwelling Units Law.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 19, 2026  7
   Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss the proposed Ordinances No. 728
  and No. 729.

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinances No. 728 and No. 729 by title
  only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO HOUSING DEVELOPMENT IN
  RESIDENTIAL ZONES

  and

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO ACCESSORY DWELLING
  UNITS AND JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinances and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinances for the next regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinances would then become effective 30 days after the adoption.

  ALTERNATIVE OPTION FOR CONSIDERATION

  Provide comments and direct staff to return at a later date with revisions to
  the amendments for the City Council’s review and approval.

  B. PROPOSED CITYWIDE FEE SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027
  [RESOLUTION NO. 26-15]

  The citywide fee schedule establishes user fees and charges for various
  department services. On an annual basis, the citywide fee schedule is reviewed
  and updated based on a combination of department input and the consumer
  price index in the Los Angeles Metro area. The proposed updated citywide fee
  schedule for Fiscal Year 2026-2027 is presented to the City Council for review,
  direction, and consideration of adoption.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 19, 2026  8
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-15 updating
  the Master Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2026-2027.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 730 AMENDING THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATED TO DOG LICENSING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HUMANE
  SOCIETY – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING; AND APPROVAL OF A
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  HUMANE SOCIETY IN THE AMOUNT OF $608,215.00

  Proposed Ordinance No. 730 would amend the City’s Municipal Code
  provisions related to dog licensing to improve efficiency, enhance compliance,
  and better align with current animal services practices. Specifically, the
  ordinance would replace the City’s existing July 1 fixed license renewal cycle
  with a rolling expiration system based on the date of the license issuance.
  Additionally, this item will consider the approval of a professional services
  agreement with the San Gabrie Valley Humane Society for an additional two
  years.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as it has no
  reasonable potential for significantly impacting the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Introduce and conduct the first reading by title only of Ordinance No. 730
  amending the San Gabriel Municipal Code to modernize the City’s dog
  licensing program by transitioning from a fixed annual renewal cycle to a
  rolling, date-based licensing structure, waive future reading, and schedule
  the second reading and adoption for the next regular City Council Meeting.

  2. Approve the Professional Services Agreement with the San Gabriel Humane
  Society of $608,215.00 for Fiscal Year 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 and
  authorize the City Manager to execute any documents necessary.

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT
